It is with great pleasure that I welcome you to The Vineyard School. Our school is nestled at the top of Richmond Hill and situated within stunning grounds. Vineyard Values
The Vineyard Vision and Values
‘Enabling all children to learn and grow’
We are a child centric school that nurtures the confidence and talents of a uniquely diverse community to instil a lifelong love of learning and create caring, resilient and curious children.
Our core values are promoted through our curriculum which has been sequentially written. This allows all children to build on the skills and knowledge they have been previously taught and supports all children to be their personal best. They form the foundation of our positive behaviour expectations and conduct of our whole community. Excellent learning, engagement and self-esteem are built through providing an environment where everyone’s contributions are recognised and valued.
Teaching, learning and wellbeing is underpinned by respect and care which we recognise as being intrinsic to both enjoyment and success at school. The strength of our progressive learning culture is based on the proactive nature and participation of all stakeholders, including our Governors, The Vineyard families and the wider community.

Music at The Vineyard
Extra Curricular Music Learning at The Vineyard
There is a thriving extracurricular music programme, most of which takes place during the school day. Lessons are mainly timed to avoid core curriculum.
The Vineyard Music Hub
Launched in September 2024, The Vineyard Music Hub is a dedicated music space offering lessons in piano, flute, musical theatre and drumkit. Our piano lessons are delivered on acoustic upright pianos, during school hours, in a dedicated teaching space. To register interest, please email music@vineyard.richmond.sch.uk.
Richmond Music Trust
We have a long-running arrangement with tutors from the Richmond Music Trust to offer 1:1 and small group voice and instrumental lessons. Currently, we offer singing, guitar, recorder, percussion and strings (violin, viola, cello, double bass) lessons. If your child is interested in having music lessons, please fill out the form which can be found here: https://www.richmondmusictrust.org.uk/site/tuition/learn-with-us/apply-now/
With Rocksteady, your child can learn to play an instrument in their very own band with no experience necessary! Guided by inspirational musicians, children learn songs they love in a fun and supportive group setting, fostering confidence, collaboration and inclusivity. Lessons take place during the school day with a performance at the end of each term. For more information click here.
The Vineyard School Orchestra
The Vineyard School Orchestra gives children in KS2 the opportunity to participate in collective music-making led by a qualified music teacher. Repertoire ranges from Vivaldi to Pirates of the Caribbean! We rehearse weekly on a Friday afternoon, and perform to parents as well as participating at larger events such as the RMT borough-wide Ensembles Day at The Exchange in Twickenham. If your child would like to join, please email music@vineyard.richmond.sch.uk. Listen here to our orchestra performing Swingle Bells arranged by D, Bellwood.
M:Tech is an exciting music technology and creativity composition course for KS2 children with sessions running on Wednesday afternoons. M:Tech is a partner of the Richmond Music Trust.
During the classes, children dive into the world of music composition, creating their own music for exciting projects including movie trailers and TV adverts. They learn about music theory in alignment with both the Vineyard and National Music Curricula and create different elements of music each session.
Every term, children receive a download of their finished music as well as a certificate to celebrate their achievement. Participation on the course also includes access to the ‘My MTech’ platform, where children can further explore their ideas and practise their skills online at home.
To register your child for the M:Tech course please visit www.mtechonline.co.uk
Before and After School Music Clubs
Our KS1 and KS2 choirs offer students a vibrant opportunity to explore the joy of singing. Rehearsals are held weekly, with children diving into a diverse repertoire that spans various genres and styles. In a fun and engaging environment, they not only enhance their vocal skills but also build confidence and teamwork. The choirs prepare for exciting performances at renowned external venues like Wembley Arena and The Rose Theatre in Kingston, fostering a love for music that lasts a lifetime.

Extra Curricular
The Vineyard School offers an engaging and exciting extracurricular timetable which complements our broad and challenging curriculum. The first full week back of clubs in September will have 86 sessions from 29 different providers.
Attending extracurricular activities boosts young people's confidence to interact socially with others; extends their social network; and provides them with new skills and abilities.
The 25/26 extracurricular timetable a layered approach. Children can transition from school to extracurricular 3:10-4:15, continue extracurricular by attending another club 4:15-5:15pm, or go home and come back for a 4:15-5:15pm club. The EDP can be booked 3:15-4:15 as a transition to a 4:15pm club.
The extracurricular timetable is not to be used for childcare. Instead, families should use the Extended Day Provision (EDP) on school site from 7:15-8:40am and 3:15pm-6:00PM
Extra Curricular timetables are released and updated each half-term the Thursday before the break at 7pm. Bookings are taken on a first come basis. A preview is released a week prior to this date. Where clubs become full and children do not get their preferred choice, families are always encouraged to contact extracurricular@vineyard.richmond.sch.uk
Snacks are allowed and welcomed at all the extracurricular options. The snack must follow the extracurricular snack policy (see attachment)
Advertisements for holiday clubs from our providers can be found in News&Events

Lunchtimes at School

Lunchtimes at School
Our aim is to encourage as many pupils as possible across the school to have a nutritious cooked school meal, a provision we are very proud of as % currently are having hot meals.
The Lunchtime Experience The school is committed to providing a welcoming dining environment that encourages positive social and cultural interactions between all of our pupils.
We are also committed to
Promoting good table manners
Providing water for everyone
ABM
As from September 2025 we are in a new catering contract with ABM. Meals are freshly cooked each day, on-site in the school kitchens.
Our chef manager and his team strive to create tasty, nutritionally balanced and culturally diverse dishes that also meet the strict healthy eating, animal welfare and food standards established by the government – meals to stimulate developing taste buds and young minds!
We are happy to introduce our operation account manager, Sue Perry with her welcome message.
If you have any concerns, queries or comments do not hesitate to contact Sue Perry via email to sperry@abmcatering.co.uk.
Pack Lunches
Most families at The Vineyard School choose for their children to have a hot school dinner. However, there is the option for children to bring in a packed lunch. We ask that the parents and carers who choose the packed lunch option for their children provide them with a healthy, well-balanced lunch. The NHS Change4life website provides tips and advice on this.
WE ARE A NUT FREE SCHOOL Any food item (snacks and packed lunches) brought in to school must be NUT FREE – we have members of staff and children on-site who suffer from severe nut allergies.
Dietary Requirements and Allergies
We believe that it is very important that every child can receive a balanced and wholesome meal irrespective of their dietary requirements. For this reason, ABM devised a procedure for special diets which ensures that their catering staff are provided with the knowledge and understanding of any specific dietary requirement and that an alternative menu can be provided where necessary.
It is very important that this special diet procedure is followed for every young person who has any food allergies or other medical requirements.
The special diet procedure and the link to our Special Diet request form. The Special Diet form must be completed for every young person with dietary requirements, by the family and returned to ABM Catering using the on-line portal, along with supporting medical evidence if requested.
Once completed, the ABM’s Menus and Diets department will create the Special Diet Menu. All information will be treated in confidence and in line with the General Data Protection Regulations.
Salad Bar
We provide a fresh salad bar alongside the main menu, with the catering team working hard to ensure that primary school favourites – such as juicy sweet peppers, tomatoes and cucumber – are available alongside new, mouth-watering combinations.
Fresh Bread
Fresh bread is baked daily, and served alongside the main menu and Salad Bar. Spencer and his team produce flavoured focaccia, ciabatta and flatbread alongside more traditional loaves. Delicious Fresh fruit platters are always available as an additional option to the day’s dessert.
Healthy Snacks at Breaktimes
We teach and promote healthy eating on the basis that a well-balanced diet can have a positive impact on children’s health, behaviour and achievement.
The suggested snacks from the policy include: apples and cheddar cheese, oatcakes and guacamole, wholemeal turkey and salad roll and much more. Please ensure you have read the policy and provide your child with a snack in line with our new policy.
WE ARE A NUT FREE SCHOOL Any food item (snacks and packed lunches) brought in to school must be NUT FREE – we have members of staff and children on-site who suffer from severe nut allergies.

Writing
Writing at The Vineyard enables our children to develop a life-long love of writing and to be equipped with the skills necessary for their future.
Through our carefully constructed curriculum, a Vineyard writer learns to:
write clearly, accurately and coherently, adapting their language and style for a range of contexts, purposes and audiences
plan, draft, revise and edit their writing to create their final piece
write with flair and creativity
communicate effectively through their writing
develop their own writer’s voice as they progress through the school
use a wide range of appropriate and ambitious vocabulary
produce work which they can be proud of
accurately form letters using The Vineyard handwriting script
use their knowledge of the different spelling patterns and common exception words to spell accurately
We teach writing through a consistent writing journey. This enables children to build their confidence and skills in every aspect of the writing process from planning, to drafting, to editing, to improving and to publishing. Our curriculum is built upon high-quality and diverse texts which engage and challenge the children.

History
History at The Vineyard provides our children with a curious awareness of Britain’s past and that of the wider world.
Through our carefully constructed curriculum, a Vineyard historian learns to:
speak like an historian, using common words and phrases linked to the passing and measuring of time
build a chronological timeline in their minds, especially from the Stone Age up to 1066
develop a broader understanding of the past to give context to key events in history
In history, we have six themes that are continuously built upon throughout our learning journey. Most units focus on world history, British history or local history. Across these units, the children will explore: lifestyles and beliefs, power, invasion, transport and legacies.
